command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Definition and notation of complex numbers
kcs.statement: Definition of complex numbers in the form $a + ib$ and $r\cos\theta + ir\sin\theta$.
kcs.raw: Definition of complex numbers in the form a + ib and r cos θ + i r sin θ.
kcs.guidance: The meaning of conjugate, modulus, argument, real part, imaginary part and equality of complex numbers should be known.

kcs.title: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
kcs.statement: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers.
kcs.raw: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers.
kcs.guidance: $|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|$. Knowledge of the result $\arg(z_1 z_2) = \arg z_1 + \arg z_2$ is not required.

kcs.title: Argand diagram representation of complex numbers
kcs.statement: Geometrical representation of complex numbers in the Argand diagram. Geometrical representation of sums, products and quotients of complex numbers.
kcs.raw: Geometrical representation of complex numbers in the Argand diagram. Geometrical representation of sums, products and quotients of complex numbers.

kcs.title: Complex roots of quadratic equations
kcs.statement: Complex solutions of quadratic equations with real coefficients.
kcs.raw: Complex solutions of quadratic equations with real coefficients.

kcs.title: Conjugate roots of cubic equations
kcs.statement: Finding conjugate complex roots and a real root of a cubic equation with integer coefficients.
kcs.raw: Finding conjugate complex roots and a real root of a cubic equation with integer coefficients.
kcs.guidance: Knowledge that if $z_1$ is a root of $f(z) = 0$ then $z_1^*$ is also a root.

kcs.title: Conjugate roots of quartic equations
kcs.statement: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic equation with real coefficients.
kcs.raw: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic equation with real coefficients.
kcs.guidance: For example, (i) $f(x) = x^4 - x^3 - 5x^2 + 7x + 10$. Given that $x = 2 + i$ is a root of $f(x) = 0$, use algebra to find the three other roots of $f(x) = 0$. (ii) $g(x) = x^4 - x^3 + 6x^2 + 14x - 20$. Given $g(1) = 0$ and $g(-2) = 0$, use algebra to solve $g(x) = 0$ completely.

kcs.title: Sum and product of quadratic roots
kcs.statement: Sum of roots and product of roots of a quadratic equation.
kcs.raw: Sum of roots and product of roots of a quadratic equation.
kcs.guidance: For the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, whose roots are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a}$, $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a}$.

kcs.title: Manipulating symmetric root expressions
kcs.statement: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and product of roots.
kcs.raw: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and product of roots.
kcs.guidance: Knowledge of the identity $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 \equiv (\alpha+\beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)$.

kcs.title: Forming quadratics with transformed roots
kcs.statement: Forming quadratic equations with new roots.
kcs.raw: Forming quadratic equations with new roots.
glossary: sum and product of new roots
kcs.guidance: For example, with roots $\alpha^3, \beta^3$; $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}, \dfrac{1}{\beta}$; $\alpha + \dfrac{2}{\alpha}, \beta + \dfrac{2}{\beta}$; etc.

kcs.title: Numerical solution of equations
kcs.statement: Equations of the form $f(x) = 0$ solved numerically by: (i) interval bisection, (ii) linear interpolation, (iii) the Newton-Raphson process.
kcs.raw: Equations of the form f(x) = 0 solved numerically by: (i) interval bisection, (ii) linear interpolation, (iii) the Newton-Raphson process.
kcs.guidance: $f(x)$ will involve only functions used in P1 and P2. For the Newton-Raphson process, the only differentiation required will be as defined in unit P1 and P2.

kcs.title: Parabola and rectangular hyperbola equations
kcs.statement: Cartesian equations for the parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
kcs.raw: Cartesian equations for the parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
kcs.guidance: Students should be familiar with the equations: $y^2 = 4ax$ or $x = at^2, y = 2at$ and $xy = c^2$ or $x = ct, y = \dfrac{c}{t}$.

kcs.title: Parametric point on the parabola
kcs.statement: Idea of parametric equation for parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
kcs.raw: Idea of parametric equation for parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
kcs.guidance: The idea of $(at^2, 2at)$ as a general point on the parabola is all that is required.

kcs.title: Focus-directrix property of the parabola
kcs.statement: The focus-directrix property of the parabola.
kcs.raw: The focus-directrix property of the parabola.
kcs.guidance: Concept of focus and directrix and parabola as locus of points equidistant from focus and directrix.

kcs.title: Tangents and normals to these curves
kcs.statement: Tangents and normals to these curves.
kcs.raw: Tangents and normals to these curves.
kcs.guidance: Differentiation of $y^2 = 4ax$ to give $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2a}{y}$, and of $xy = c^2$ to give $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{c^2}{x^2}$. Parametric differentiation is not required.

kcs.title: Addition and subtraction of matrices
kcs.statement: Addition and subtraction of matrices.
kcs.raw: Addition and subtraction of matrices.

kcs.title: Scalar multiplication of a matrix
kcs.statement: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar.
kcs.raw: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar.

kcs.title: Multiplying matrices together
kcs.statement: Products of matrices.
kcs.raw: Products of matrices.

kcs.title: Evaluating 2x2 determinants
kcs.statement: Evaluation of $2 \times 2$ determinants.
kcs.raw: Evaluation of 2 × 2 determinants.
kcs.guidance: Singular and non-singular matrices.

kcs.title: Inverse of 2x2 matrices
kcs.statement: Inverse of $2 \times 2$ matrices.
kcs.raw: Inverse of 2 × 2 matrices.
kcs.guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

kcs.title: Matrix representation of linear transformations
kcs.statement: Linear transformations of column vectors in two dimensions and their matrix representation.
kcs.raw: Linear transformations of column vectors in two dimensions and their matrix representation.
kcs.guidance: The transformation represented by $AB$ is the transformation represented by $B$ followed by the transformation represented by $A$.

kcs.title: Matrices for geometric transformations
kcs.statement: Applications of $2 \times 2$ matrices to represent geometrical transformations.
kcs.raw: Applications of 2 × 2 matrices to represent geometrical transformations.
kcs.guidance: Identification and use of the matrix representation of single transformations from: reflection in coordinate axes and lines $y = \pm x$; rotation through any angle about $(0,0)$; stretches parallel to the $x$-axis and $y$-axis; and enlargement about centre $(0,0)$ with scale factor $k$ ($k \neq 0$), where $k \in \mathbb{R}$.

kcs.title: Combining matrix transformations
kcs.statement: Combinations of transformations.
kcs.raw: Combinations of transformations.
kcs.guidance: Identification and use of the matrix representation of combined transformations.

kcs.title: Inverse of combined transformations
kcs.statement: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.
kcs.raw: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.
kcs.guidance: Idea of the determinant as an area scale factor in transformations.

kcs.title: Summing simple finite series
kcs.statement: Summation of simple finite series.
kcs.raw: Summation of simple finite series.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to sum series such as $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r^2$, $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r^3$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r(r+2)$. The method of differences is not required.

kcs.title: Proof by mathematical induction
kcs.statement: Proof by mathematical induction.
kcs.raw: Proof by mathematical induction.
kcs.guidance: To include induction proofs for (i) summation of series, e.g. show $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^n r^3 = \dfrac{1}{4}n^2(n+1)^2$ or $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^n r(r+1) = \dfrac{1}{3}n(n+1)(n+2)$ (ii) divisibility, e.g. show $3^{2n+1} + 1$ is divisible by 4 (iii) finding general terms in a sequence, e.g. if $u_{n+1} = 3u_n + 4$ with $u_1 = 1$, prove that $u_n = 3^n - 2$ (iv) matrix products, e.g. show that $A^n$ for a given $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ can be found in terms of $n$.
